newsitem.title: UK: London gold may rally after IMF does nothing.
newsitem.headline: London gold may rally after IMF does nothing.

text.p: The gold market was standing by for a price surge on Thursday after speculators took positions favouring a go-ahead for the sale of International Monetary Fund (IMF) gold which failed to materialise.
"At some point the funds are going to have to react. And then everyone's going to cover like crazy," a dealer said, adding that gold could soar up to $388 an ounce.

A dealer referring to an IMF proposal to sell five million ounces of gold from its reserves to aid the poorest countries said, "Most people were saying a decision wasn't going to be made, and it's completely irrelevant to the market anyway."
Bullion was fixed little changed at $383.10 an ounce from $383.00 on Wednesday evening and a London close of $383.35.
Gold prices eased last week after U.S. investment funds took short positions ahead of IMF meetings on the plan, playing on fears prices would drop if fresh gold supply hit the market.
"There's still room to the downside, but not that much," one said. On the charts gold was looking steadier after breaking above a three-week-old downtrend line earlier this week.
Analysts noted that in the longer term, gold was moving into the peak demand season, covering Christmas buying in the West and post-monsoon and wedding buying in Asia.
Silver prices were also little changed from London closing levels, just two cents lower at $5.07 an ounce.
Platinum was hovering around its closing price near the the $390 resistance level, after notching up about $2 on Wednesday.
Its sister metal palladium was slightly stronger at $121.75 an ounce after dropping to three-year lows earlier this week.
